_comment: Example broker configuration. This file lives on the HOST, outside every path the agent
container can see, and it is the one place that decides which repositories may receive a
Required keys: socketPath, hosts. Everything else is optional.
Only top-level '_comment*' keys are ignored. The 'hosts' object is validated strictly on
purpose: every entry must be a real host with a known provider and a non-empty allowlist,
so a typo cannot sit there looking like configuration while doing nothing.
See the README's configuration reference for every field.
_comment_socketMode: Octal, written in decimal. 432 = 0660, right when broker uid == container uid.
_comment_auditPath: Append-only JSONL, deliberately unreadable from the container. Records grants and refusals, never credentials.
_comment_tokenCacheSkewSeconds: Re-mint a cached token this many seconds before it expires.
_comment_hosts: Each entry is keyed by the host exactly as git reports it: 'github.com' (no port) or
'host:port' for a non-default port. Provider is 'github-app' or 'static'.
'allow' is default-deny and matched per path segment: 'owner/repo', 'owner/*'. There is
no prefix matching, so 'acme/widget' can never authorize 'acme/widget-evil'. A malformed
entry (no slash, three segments, a partial wildcard like 'wid*') is rejected at startup
'allowInsecureHttp' defaults to false. Set it true only for a plaintext remote you trust;
it is read here, host-side, so nothing in the container can widen it.
'permissions' must be a subset of what the app itself was granted. The broker checks this
once via GET /app and fails with a message naming the missing permission, because GitHub
answers 422 for an ungranted request and that is easy to misread as a broker fault.
Set 'verifyAppPermissions': false to skip that check (e.g. against a mocked API).

github.com._comment_identity: clientId is preferred as the JWT `iss`; appId is the fallback. The client secret is NOT used and is not needed anywhere.
github.com._userTokens: optional: fine-grained tokens keyed by owner, used only to create pull requests
github.com._comment_permissions: Must not exceed the app's own grant. Grant 'Pull requests: Read and write' in the app settings first if you want the agent to open PRs.
